video.title: Combined and Regional School Committee Meeting / September 16, 2026

summary.body: Northborough School Committee, Southborough School Committee, Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee, and Superintendency Union No. 3
summary.headline: School committees approved a $22,750 salary adjustment for the superintendent and reviewed the district strategic plan and high school cell phone protocols.
summary.summary: Meeting jointly and separately, the school committees of Northborough, Southborough, and the Regional District reviewed the district's updated Vision 2032 strategic plan and the superintendent's annual evaluation goals. Following an executive session, all four bodies approved a $22,750 market salary adjustment for Superintendent Gregory Martineau, bringing his base salary to $270,213 for the 2026-2027 school year. In its separate session, the Regional School Committee received updates on high school cell phone protocols, including pausing the rollout of the third-party Doorman app amid technical and privacy concerns, and accepted $47,000 in educational grants.

topics.title: Vision 2032 district strategic plan presentation
topics.summary: District administrators presented Vision 2032, the successor strategic plan to Vision 2026, which outlines educational priorities across ten schools in three districts. The presentation detailed five core objectives: empowering learners, fostering belonging and student success, promoting healthy and balanced learners, cultivating educator leadership, and maintaining sound finance and operations.
key_details: Vision 2026 initiatives reached between 64% and 85% completion across major strategic objectives.
Vision 2032 integrates artificial intelligence, digital wellness, and adaptability into instructional frameworks.
The district plans a baseline student belonging survey aiming for at least 80% student participation in spring 2027.
Curriculum initiatives include quarter learning walks, digital citizenship coursework, and environmental sustainability goals.

topics.title: Superintendent 2026-2027 evaluation goals and timeline
topics.summary: The superintendent presented proposed goals for the 2026-2027 school year aligned with Vision 2032, major capital initiatives, and administrative transition planning. The schedule sets a progress update for December 2, 2026, member evaluations due in May 2027, and a public evaluation presentation on June 14, 2027.
key_details: Major focus areas include advancing the Neary School project in Southborough and the Peaslee School project in Northborough.
Goals align with assistant superintendents and building leadership teams to ensure districtwide continuity.
Superintendent planned a mid-cycle progress report to the combined committees on December 2, 2026.
topics.outcome: Approved unanimously across all four committees.

topics.title: 2027-2028 school calendar discussion
topics.summary: Committees discussed the framework for building the 2027-2028 academic calendar, focusing on how religious holidays are scheduled and the impact on the school year end date. Members debated options including maintaining the current holiday structure, removing specific religious holidays, adjusting school start dates, or modifying February and April vacations to prevent the school year extending late into June.
key_details: Committees considered whether to keep the holiday schedule stable for a three-year cycle before making changes.
Concerns were raised that five snow days push the end of the school year past June 25, affecting attendance and exams.
Superintendent will work with committee chairs and gather feedback ahead of a formal calendar proposal in December.
topics.outcome: Discussed; administration will develop options and feedback mechanisms for the December 2, 2026 meeting.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: Committees approved open and executive session minutes from June 15, 2026, April 7, 2026, June 17, 2026, and August 11, 2026. The Regional School Committee also reappointed Matt Spencer as District Assistant Treasurer, appointed Kathleen Harragan as voting delegate to the Massachusetts Association of School Committees annual meeting, and appointed John Winske to the Stipend Review Committee.
key_details: Kathleen Harragan appointed MASC voting delegate for the November 6, 2026 conference in Danvers.
Matt Spencer reappointed District Assistant Treasurer for 2026-2027.
John Winske appointed regional school committee representative to the Stipend Review Committee.
topics.outcome: All routine minutes, appointments, and committee assignments approved unanimously.

topics.title: Superintendent contract market salary adjustment
topics.summary: Following an executive session, the committees reconvened to act on a proposed market adjustment for Superintendent Gregory Martineau's employment contract, which runs through the 2027-2028 school year. All four committees approved a base salary adjustment of $22,750 for the 2026-2027 school year, retroactive to July 1, 2026.
key_details: Base salary increases from $247,463 to $270,213 for the 2026-2027 school year.
Adjustment is retroactive to July 1, 2026.
Officials stated the adjustment will not require tax increases and will be absorbed within existing approved district budgets.
Adjustment was justified based on comparative compensation in peer districts and long-term succession planning.
topics.outcome: Approved by Superintendency Union No. 3 (6-0), Northborough School Committee (4-1), Southborough School Committee (5-0), and Regional School Committee (unanimous).
topics.why_it_matters: Changes superintendent compensation using town school budget allocations across Northborough and Southborough.

topics.title: Regional high school opening update and operations
topics.summary: Regional school administration delivered opening updates for Algonquin Regional High School covering staffing, operations, technology, and summer programs. Officials reported 1,212 enrolled students, 16 new regional staff hires with low professional turnover, fully staffed bus routes, and the installation of interactive digital display boards across 110 classrooms.
key_details: All 32 school buses had trained drivers in place for the opening of the school year.
Algonquin enrollment stood at 1,212 students, with 283 freshmen, 312 sophomores, 321 juniors, and 296 seniors.
Interactive Newline touchscreens were fully installed in 110 high school classrooms and science lab projectors were updated.
District email security implemented anti-phishing software that blocked over 8,000 phishing attempts in its first four weeks.
The high school doubled its internet bandwidth from 1 gigabit to 2 gigabits.
topics.outcome: Information received; no committee action required.

topics.title: FY26 budget closeout and FY27 budget update
topics.summary: Director of Finance and Operations Rebecca Pellegrino presented the final closeout of the FY26 regional budget and an initial report on FY27. The regional district closed FY26 with a general fund surplus of $431,947, which reverts to the Excess and Deficiency reserve, and certified an estimated E&D balance of $1,144,256, representing 3.25% to 3.75% of the operating budget.
key_details: FY26 closeout surplus of $431,947 returned to the district Excess and Deficiency account.
State circuit breaker extraordinary relief provided nearly $400,000 in tuition reimbursement and $17,000 in transportation relief in FY26.
Estimated certified E&D balance stands at $1,144,256, aligning with school committee reserve policy.
FY27 operating budget shows a remaining available balance of $860,460 (2.74%) two months into the fiscal year.
topics.outcome: Regional School Committee voted unanimously to approve FY26 closeout transfers, revenue reports, student activity balances, and FY27 line-item transfers and revenue reports.
topics.why_it_matters: Sets the final certified reserves for the regional district and manages taxpayer-funded balances between fiscal years.

topics.title: Food services update and Whitsons action plan
topics.summary: Director of Operations Keith Lavoie reported on menu changes and service adjustments made by food service vendor Whitsons in response to student and parent feedback from the previous spring. The vendor restored popular menu items, adjusted portion sides to comply with national lunch program standards, and appointed Christina Blake as the new district general manager.
key_details: The original Algonquin cookie recipe was restored and made available daily.
Whitsons added meal side options, pasta dishes, burritos, and ramen to increase entree substance and variety.
A new district dietician is engaging directly with students across high school and middle school cafeterias.
Christina Blake begins as Whitsons general manager for the district next week.
topics.outcome: Report accepted; a quarterly update on student participation and finances will be provided in December.

topics.title: Algonquin high school international travel to Spain
topics.summary: Administrators provided follow-up details regarding the planned student trip to Spain scheduled for April 2027 through EF Tours. The district confirmed insurance coverage through both EF Tours and the district carrier, outlined emergency repatriation protocols, and explained unsupervised student time guidelines in group settings.
key_details: Thirty students were selected by lottery from 54 applicants, with a waitlist established.
EF Tours policy includes global travel protection covering medical emergencies, trip cancellations, and emergency chaperones.
Unsupervised free time during lunches will require students to travel in groups of at least four with mandatory mobile phone contact.
Fundraising and scholarship opportunities through EF Tours will be explored with families in November.
topics.outcome: Information accepted; organizers will provide updated plans closer to the departure date.

topics.title: High school cell phone protocol and Doorman app pause
topics.summary: Principal Sean Bevan updated the committee on efforts to regulate student cell phone use, announcing a pause on the planned implementation of the Doorman geofencing mobile app. While classroom phone cubbies remain in place, administration delayed the app rollout due to technical release delays on the principal's test device as well as data privacy and surveillance concerns raised by students and parents.
key_details: Algonquin will continue using in-classroom 'off-and-away' canvas caddies while longer-term options are studied.
MetroWest adolescent health survey showed local daily smartphone use over three hours rose from 50.6% in 2021 to 65.4% in 2025.
Forty percent of Algonquin students screened at or above the threshold for problematic internet use.
Rollout of the Doorman app was placed on indefinite hold to evaluate technical performance, student input, and community consensus.
State legislation restricting bell-to-bell phone use remains stalled in a legislative conference committee.
topics.outcome: Administration paused app rollout and will gather further student and community input through the steering committee.
topics.why_it_matters: Directly affects daily student routines, classroom learning environments, and student digital privacy policies.

topics.title: Approval of educational grants
topics.summary: The Regional School Committee considered and accepted two educational grants awarded to the district. These include a state Department of Elementary and Secondary Education grant for genocide education and a community health foundation grant supporting student wellness data initiatives.
key_details: Accepted a $41,000 DESE Genocide Education Grant for staff curriculum development and instruction.
Accepted a $6,000 grant from the MetroWest Health Foundation supporting responsive work around student health survey data.
topics.outcome: Voted unanimously to accept both grants.

public_comment.summary: A Northborough resident thanked the committees for maintaining religious holiday observances on the current calendar and urged them to continue including major Jewish holidays, while also suggesting revisiting anti-bias and anti-discrimination initiatives.

A resident and chair of the Northborough Appropriations Committee proposed holding earlier joint discussions during the budget cycle so municipal financial committees and the school district share common terminology and budget assumptions.

A Northborough resident expressed opposition to the Doorman phone management application, arguing that installing monitoring applications on personal phones violates student privacy and existing committee policy, and noted that pending state legislation on cell phones remains unresolved.

A Southborough resident argued that school committees, rather than school staff, have legal responsibility for setting cell phone policies and raised concerns about data security audits and VPN requirements associated with third-party software vendors.

A special education advocate criticized the district's seclusion and physical restraint policies, called for parent input from the Special Education Parent Advisory Council, and alleged an Open Meeting Law violation regarding meeting livestreams.
An Algonquin junior expressed relief that the Doorman application rollout was suspended, citing peer concerns regarding data security risks and the protection of student personal information.
A resident speaker reiterated concerns regarding student seclusion policies, cybersecurity risks in school email systems, and public records access.
